subject: Learning Methods
title: Selective Attention
description: A quick, practical guide to Selective Attention.

hook.text: In a famous experiment, half the viewers missed a gorilla walking through a basketball game they were watching.

buildup.text: Selective attention lets you focus on one input while filtering out everything else around you.

discovery.text: Your brain cannot process everything. It picks a target and suppresses the rest to conserve resources.

twist.text: The gorilla study proved that filtering is so strong you can miss obvious events right in front of you.

climax.text: Selective attention is a feature, not a bug. Without it, every stimulus would compete equally for your focus.

punchline.text: You see what you focus on. Everything else vanishes.

quiz.question: What does the invisible gorilla experiment demonstrate?
options: People have poor vision under stress
Selective attention can make you miss obvious events
